subject: Money
title: No Taxation Without Representation
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on No Taxation Without Representation.

hook.text: In 1773, colonists dumped 342 chests of tea into Boston Harbor. The tax was only three pence per pound.

buildup.text: Britain taxed its American colonies without giving them seats in Parliament. Revenue without voice.

discovery.text: The principle: if you pay taxes, you deserve a say in how they're spent. Consent matters.

twist.text: Washington D.C. residents pay federal tax but have no voting members of Congress. The fight continues.

climax.text: Taxation without representation started a revolution. The idea that money buys voice is foundational.

punchline.text: The Boston Tea Party was a tax protest.

quiz.question: What triggered the Boston Tea Party?
